text: 3. The real scope-changer: regenerating `ActionBuilders.generated.swift` (`cargo run -p nmp-codegen -- gen action-builders --platform swift`, run from the pinned NMP checkout — this DOES drop `visibleNoteRelations`, confirming the dead builder is gone from the current registry) also removes four OTHER builder functions Chirp iOS/Android still call: `zap`, `postComment`, `topicArticles`, and `createPublicGroup` (renamed to `createGroup`, matching the NIP-29 rename I already handled on the Rust side for tui/desktop). Real call sites exist in `apps/ios/Chirp/Bridge/KernelBridge+PublishOperations.swift`, `apps/ios/Chirp/Bridge/PublicGroupBridge.swift`, and `apps/android/.../SocialActions.kt`. Two new builders were added too (`editGroupMetadata`, `reply` — the last maybe subsuming `postComment`, unconfirmed). I haven't looked at what changed in `zap`'s and `postComment`'s underlying shape/namespace yet. [...] **Your question D, answered precisely:** each app runs `flatc` itself and checks the output in locally for the FlatBuffers wire-type decoders (`OpFeedSnapshot` et al.) — NMP does not ship a prebuilt bindings package for iOS, Android, or web on this front (no regen script exists anywhere in Chirp's repo for it, a real process gap worth closing as part of chirp#35). This is DIFFERENT from action-builders: iOS/Android's `ActionBuilders.generated.*` ARE regeneratable via the documented `cargo run -p nmp-codegen -- gen action-builders --platform swift/kotlin` command. Web is different again — its action builders come from the external `@nmp/runtime-web` npm package (not a local generated file at all), so web's action-builders migration is entirely gated on that package publishing, same as web's FlatBuffers-decode fix (both blocked on the NMP#2497 / rc.2 publish you flagged).
